metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe registry mirror --json` (PROP-002 `#registry-mirror`): which versions of the source registry a run copied into the target `monorepo` / `localdir`, which it found unchanged, which it refused, and the commit it made. Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/registry_mirror_report.rs`.
False iff any version is an `alarm` (then nothing was written) or `unavailable` (the others were copied).
Always `"registry:mirror"` for this report.
The `[[registry]].name` mirrored from.
Its url (credentials redacted).
Where the source's version list came from.
The target: repository url (credentials redacted) and branch, a working copy, or a directory.
Every source version the filters selected, sorted by package then version.
Journal facts the run recorded in the target (a publication per copied version, plus carried-over yanks and tombstones); on a dry run, the facts it would record.
The target's registry index was rewritten (on a dry run: would be).
`monorepo`: a non-fast-forward rejection was absorbed by one refetch and retry.
`--keep-history`: history bundles written (or, on a dry run, that would be); 0 without the flag.
The commit made: pushed for a `monorepo`, local for a `working-copy`. Absent when nothing changed, on a dry run, for a `localdir`, and when an alarm stopped the run.

One row per `[[template]]` row of the selection (PROP-075 `#MIRROR-CONFIG`), in selection order: what it selected, what the snapshot now carries, and — with `payloads = true` — the payload projection it would write or wrote. Absent for a run with no template row, which is every mirror run that predates the feature.
How many of the `pruned[]` rows this run removed. Zero when the plan was printed and not answered yes, and on a dry run; absent without `--prune`.

One row per removal `--prune` planned (PROP-075 `#MIRROR-PRUNE`): what went, from where, and the reason that reached it. It is the **plan**, which is printed before anything is removed and is never silent; `removed` says how many of its rows this run actually took out, which is none on a dry run and none when the plan's question was answered no. Absent without `--prune`, because no run without it ever deletes anything.
An exact non-negative byte count. JTD has no uint64 form, so generated Rust narrows the numeric form to u64.
The channel name the `[[template]]` row asked for.
The newest member of the channel's set — what the channel lowers to. Absent when the template declares no such channel, which selects nothing and is reported rather than refused.
The `[[installer_options]]` id the render dropped.
The file upstream does not publish for this version, which is why a `template_optional` row was dropped instead of failing the render (PROP-075 `#TEMPLATE-OPTION-GATING`).

The installer options kept for this version, in manifest order — what `platforms` / `archs` / `installers` resolved to against the rendered manifest. Present only for a row with `payloads = true`, which is the only row that reads the options at all.
Payload inputs those options declare.
Of them, the ones already in the drop with the right digest, which are counted and never fetched again.
Payload inputs the selected versions and options declare.
Of them, the ones already in the drop with the right digest.
Declared bytes already in the drop.
Declared bytes to fetch — what `[payloads] max_total` is checked against, before the first byte is written.
`present_bytes` + `fetch_bytes`. A **lower bound** when `unknown` is non-zero: a template that declares no `size` for an input cannot be weighed, and the total says so rather than guessing.
Inputs whose size the rendered manifest does not declare (`PROP-065#sizes`), which is what makes `total_bytes` a lower bound.

The `[payloads] into` drop the projection writes at `<into>/<group>/<name>/<version>/<file>`, the first rung of the drop lookup (PROP-066 `#drops`). The one place a mirror run writes outside the registry target.
`<group>/<name>` of the template package.
The template package's own version — a revision, never a produced version.
Produced versions the row selected: what `versions` matched unioned with the members of every `channels` entry, then `newest = N` per major.
Of them, the ones this run added to the snapshot (on a dry run: would add).
Of them, the ones the snapshot already carried and this run left untouched.
The selected versions, oldest first — the children of the row's node in the human form.
Every channel the row named and what it resolved to.
The `template_optional` rows the render dropped, each naming the file upstream does not publish.
The oldest selected version; absent when the row selected nothing, which is reported and is not an error.
The newest selected version.
The installer-option ids the row asks to keep, as authored. They select nothing in the snapshot itself — a version's inputs are per version, not per option — and are what payload projection acts on.
The payload projection of this row; absent unless the row carries `payloads = true`.

`version`: a package version directory in the target; `snapshot`: a template snapshot under `_index/`, whole or by version; `payload`: a projected payload in the drop, the one removal outside the registry — it happens after the commit that stops advertising it. Closed: automation decides from it whether a removal changed the registry or only the drop.
`<group>/<name>` the removal belongs to.

Registry-relative for a `version` or a `snapshot`, the absolute drop path for a `payload`. It spells the coordinate of its fact: a `version` path is exactly `<group>/<name>/v<version>`, which is what lets the batch refuse a removal that claims a coordinate it is not (PROP-075 `#MIRROR-PRUNE`).
Why this removal reached the plan — "no longer selected by `[select]`", "no longer selected by `[[template]]` <package>".
The version removed; absent for a whole snapshot or a whole package's payloads, which carry no single version.

`index`: the source registry's package index (`primary.jsonl`); `layout`: a `monorepo` / `localdir` source's own tree and index; `tags`: the `v<version>` tags of the packages named by `--package` (a source without an index); `api`: the repositories the host's organisation listing names (`GET /orgs/<org>/repos` on GitHub or GitVerse), filtered to those whose name the registry's naming convention claims and that carry a `vibe.toml` with a `[package]` at a `v<version>` tag, each then read by its tags. Closed: a reader decides from it whether unchanged versions were compared by the source's recorded hash or by fetching.
`monorepo`: a repository url, cloned, committed and pushed; `working-copy`: a local Git working copy, committed into and not pushed; `localdir`: a directory registry, written in place.

`copied`: new in the target (on a dry run: would be); `updated`: a snapshot version whose content moved at the source, replaced because `--update-snapshots` was given; `unchanged`: the target already holds the same content; `snapshot-differs`: a snapshot version whose content moved at the source, left as it is (pass `--update-snapshots`); `alarm`: a frozen version whose content differs, or bytes that disagree with the source's own index — refused, and the whole run with it; `unavailable`: the source could not serve the version (its repository or tag is missing or denied) — the others are still copied and the run exits non-zero. Closed: automation decides from it whether the target changed and whether to page someone.
`<group>/<name>`.
The version is frozen (at the source or in the target): its bytes may never change.
The source withdrew the version; the fact is carried into the target's journal.
The content hash the source records (or, without an index, the fetched tree's).
The source ref the bytes were read at (a tag, or a monorepo branch).
The source commit, recorded in the target as the version's provenance.
Why a version is `snapshot-differs`, `alarm` or `unavailable`.

The Git tree of the source commit. For a `copied` / `updated` version written by this run, the version directory's Git tree hash was checked equal to it before anything was committed (`tree_verified`).
True when this run wrote the version and checked its directory's Git tree hash equal to `tree`. Absent when nothing was written or the source is not Git (a layout source).
